title: A finite algebra over a henselian local ring is a product of henselian local rings
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and $R\to B$ a ring map making $B$ a finitely generated $R$-module. Then there are an integer $r\ge0$, local rings $(B_1,\mathfrak n_1),\dots,(B_r,\mathfrak n_r)$, each an $R$-algebra and a finitely generated $R$-module, and an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $B\cong B_1\times\dots\times B_r$ ($B=0$ if $r=0$), such that for every $i$: $B_i$ is a henselian local ring, and $R\to B_i$ is a local homomorphism ($\mathfrak n_i\cap R=\mathfrak m$, the preimage of $\mathfrak n_i$ in $R$ being $\mathfrak m$), so that $B_i/\mathfrak n_i$ is a finite field extension of $\kappa$ [def-pc-field-extension].

source.place: Lemma Tag 04GH (lemma-finite-over-henselian) (1) and (2), and its proof: '(2) implies (1) since S as in (1) is a finite product of its localizations at the primes lying over m by Lemma 04GG (10); (2) also follows from 04GG (10) since any finite S-algebra is also a finite R-algebra (any finite ring map between local rings is local)'

proof.text: *Product of local factors.* The henselian hypothesis gives the etale retraction property of [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-etale-retraction]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-etale-retraction-finite-product-local] to the finite $R$-algebra $B$ therefore gives an $R$-algebra isomorphism $B\cong B_1\times\cdots\times B_r$ (with the empty product when $B=0$), where every $B_i$ is local. Each factor is a finitely generated $R$-module because it is the image of $B$ under a product projection.

source.place: Lemma Tag 04GH (lemma-finite-over-henselian), (1), using the proof of Lemma Tag 04GG (8) => (10)

proof.text: *The factors are local over $R$ and have finite residue extensions.* For each local factor $(B_i,\mathfrak n_i)$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-local-radical] applied to the finite map $R\to B_i$ says that the preimage of $\mathfrak n_i$ is $\mathfrak m$; hence $R\to B_i$ is local. Choose finitely many $R$-module generators of $B_i$. Their classes generate $B_i/\mathfrak n_i$ as a vector space over $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$, because $\mathfrak mB_i\subseteq\mathfrak n_i$. Thus $B_i/\mathfrak n_i$ is a finite-dimensional $\kappa$-algebra which is a field (as $B_i$ is local), so it is a finite field extension of $\kappa$ [def-pc-field-extension].

source.place: Lemma Tag 04GH, clauses (1) and (2): each factor is finite over $R$, the map is local, and the residue field is finite over $\kappa$

proof.text: *Each factor is henselian.* Fix $i$ and let $C$ be a finite $B_i$-algebra. By transitivity of finite generation, $C$ is also a finite $R$-algebra. The retraction property from [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-etale-retraction] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-retraction-finite-product-local] give $C\cong\prod_j C_j$ with each $C_j$ local. Every $C_j$ is a finite $B_i$-algebra, being a product projection of the finite $B_i$-algebra $C$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-local-radical] to the finite map $B_i\to C_j$ shows that the preimage in $B_i$ of the maximal ideal of $C_j$ is $\mathfrak n_i$; consequently $\mathfrak n_iC_j$ is contained in that maximal ideal and $C_j/\mathfrak n_iC_j$ is local. A local ring has only the idempotents $0$ and $1$, and idempotents of a finite product are componentwise. Therefore every idempotent of $C/\mathfrak n_iC\cong\prod_j(C_j/\mathfrak n_iC_j)$ is a $0$-$1$ vector, and it has exactly one lift, the same $0$-$1$ vector in $C\cong\prod_jC_j$. This is the idempotent-lifting definition of $B_i$ being henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology].

source.place: Lemma Tag 04GH, clause (2) and proof: a finite algebra over a local factor is finite over $R$, and the product-of-local-rings criterion gives the henselian idempotent lifting
